[[Newark, New Jersey]] | awards = * Second Team [[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] (2011) * 2× [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|OVC Player of the Year]] * 2010 AP honorable mention All-American * 2010 OVC Defensive Player of the Year * 2x First Team All-OVC (2009, 2010) * MVP, 2009 OVC Tournament | tournaments = Y | tournament_list = * 2x NCAA ([[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011]]) * 1x [[College Basketball Invitational]] ([[2010 College Basketball Invitational|2010]]) | championships = Y | championship_list = *2x OVC Men's Basketball Tournament ([[2009 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2011 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2011]]) }} '''Kenneth Bernard Faried Lewis''' (born November 18, 1989), commonly known as '''Kenneth Faried''', is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. He was a forward-center at [[Morehead State University]], where he was named [[Ohio Valley Conference]] [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] and an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2010. ==High school career== Faried attended [[Technology High School (New Jersey)|Technology High School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]].{{cite news | url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=6101092 | title=Kenneth Faried adapts and thrives | first=Dana | last=O'Neil | work=[[ESPN.com]] | date=February 9, 2011 | accessdate=March 20, 2011}} He received recruiting interest from [[Marist College|Marist]] and [[Iona College (New York)|Iona]] colleges in [[New York]], but chose to attend [[Morehead State University]] in [[Morehead, Kentucky]]. ==College career== Faried, a 6'8 (2.03 m) post player, came to Morehead State in 2007 and became one of the best players in school and conference history. Faried led the Ohio Valley Conference in [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] as both a sophomore and junior (13.0 rebounds per game in each season) – ranking him third in the [[NCAA]] in [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09]] and second in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]]. Faried also chipped in double-digit scoring in each of his three varsity seasons.[http://www.msueagles.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1433&path=mbball], accessed October 15, 2010 Faried also led the Eagles to team success, as Morehead claimed a berth in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]] by winning the [[2009 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Ohio Valley conference tournament]]. Faried led the way, scoring 15 points and grabbing 17 rebounds in the final against [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]], and was named tournament [[Most Valuable Player]]. In his junior year, Faried again led the Eagles to the post-season as they advanced to the second round of the [[College Basketball Invitational]]. At the end of the season, Faried was named OVC player and defensive player of the year and an [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].[http://www.msueagles.com/news/2010/3/29/MBB_0329101455.aspx?path=mbball Faried Named AP All-America Honorable Mention], accessed October 15, 2010 He also passed 1000 rebounds for his career. After his junior season, Faried declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA Draft]]. However, he elected to return for his senior season, pulling out on May 7, 2010.[http://www.ovcsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=31039&SPID=2443&DB_OEM_ID=6200&ATCLID=204942482 Morehead State's Faried to Return For Senior Season], accessed October 15, 2010] Faried broke [[Tim Duncan]]'s modern-era (post-1973) Division I career rebounding mark with 12 rebounds in the Eagles' 71–65 victory over [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]] on February 19, 2011. The NCAA's modern era began after 1973 when freshmen were permitted to play along with the split into the three divisions in use today. Duncan's previous record of 1,570 rebounds had stood since 1997. In his senior season, Faried was named a second-team [[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] and by [[Fox Sports]].{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports]]||publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}}[http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2011/allamerica110314.html USBWA names 2010-11 All-Americans], accessed March 17, 2011 On April 1, 2011, Faried was named the most valuable player of the Reese's college all-star game.{{cite web|title=Kenneth Faried boosts West all-stars|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6282141|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|accessdate=2 April 2011|date=1 April|year=2011}} ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
